# Privacy allowlist (see scripts/privacy_scan.py --allow).
# One regular expression per line, optional "# reason" suffix.
#
# Each entry is one fully escaped, anchored literal: no class, no wildcard, no
# alternation. A new secret is fixed at source and never added here. There are two
# entries, one per quoted path family that cannot be reworded: the pi install tree
# and the operator user name (D-20261019-CEO-8, D-20261019-CEO-15).
#
# What an entry exempts is exactly one finding VALUE, not a directory: the scanner
# tests each match against the pattern, and for `home-path` that value is the user
# name alone. So `^\.pi/agent/npm$` covers every `agent-config` finding whose value
# is that install tree, and `^/home/pingz$` covers every `home-path` finding for that
# one user name - whether the path ends there, at `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, or anywhere else
# under it. A credential rule is unaffected by either entry: a token, key or
# password on the same line is still reported, and a sibling user name does not
# match.

# ^\.pi/agent/npm$ - opened by T-0001. The quoted pi-subagents install path: the
# scanner's own fixture at tests/unit/test_privacy_scan.py, the pre-fix blob of
# references/Adapters.md and the audit quotations of it in history, so `--tree`
# alone is red by design. Rewriting that unpublished history would invalidate
# commit SHAs quoted as evidence in docs/Team/Archive.md and docs/Team/Decisions.md.
# Nothing from package-lock.json is blessed: the scanner does not report its
# "resolved" tarball URLs.
^\.pi/agent/npm$

# ^/home/pingz$ - the operator user name, which appears as a build path in one
# archived reviewer finding and in the justification text of this file. The
# exemption is fixed by SHAPE (one literal user name), never by count: the number
# of historical blobs that quote it grows with every commit that documents it.
# A user name is not a credential, which is why this shape - and nothing else - is
# exempted; anything secret on such a line is still caught by its own rule.
^/home/pingz$
